title: GPU Autoscaling on Kubernetes — Karpenter, KAI Scheduler, Gang Scheduling

questions.question: Which signal does the QUEUE_DEPTH strategy inspect when deciding to add replicas?
options: The number of requests waiting in queue
DCGM GPU utilization only
The number of completed tokens yesterday
The model's parameter count
questions.explanation: The strategy reads len(queue), adding capacity when the actual request backlog exceeds its threshold.

questions.question: With KAI_GANG and a queue depth of 7, how many replicas does the strategy request in that tick?
options: One, because KAI never scales in pairs
Two, from max(2, qd // 3)
Seven, one for each queued request
Four, from qd // 2
questions.explanation: For qd > 3, KAI_GANG adds max(2, qd // 3); at qd=7 this is max(2,2)=2 replicas.

questions.question: When does simulate mark a queued request as dropped?
options: After 15 seconds, at every HPA tick
As soon as GPU utilization falls below 20%
When now - arrived_at exceeds 30 seconds
Only after MAX_REPLICAS is reached
questions.explanation: The queue loop applies the explicit SLA timeout if now - arrived_at exceeds 30, then marks the request dropped.

questions.question: A new replica in this simulator becomes ready after which combined delay?
options: 15 seconds of HPA delay only
45 seconds of model load only
110 seconds of cluster autoscaler plus 45 seconds
50 + 45 = 95 seconds
questions.explanation: pending_replicas receive ready_at = now + NODE_PROVISION_SEC + MODEL_LOAD_SEC = 50 + 45 seconds; the cluster autoscaler constant is only a comparison.

questions.question: Which Karpenter policy is described as safe for running jobs in the lesson?
options: WhenEmpty with consolidateAfter: 1h
WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized with no delay
Terminate every node below 70% GPU utilization
Scale down whenever queue depth is nonzero
questions.explanation: The lesson warns that WhenEmptyOrUnderutilized can terminate active jobs and recommends WhenEmpty plus a one-hour consolidation delay.

questions.question: Why is DUTY_CYCLE a misleading default signal for this LLM workload?
options: It cannot observe any Kubernetes object
Backlog is the useful signal
It always adds 16 replicas at once
It measures queue depth twice and drops every request
questions.explanation: The demo contrasts DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL with backlog-aware scaling: a memory-bound or queued LLM can have misleading duty-cycle readings.
